title: TII Releases Falcon-ASR: 1.6B Arabic Speech Model Hits 20.92% WER
source_used: MarkTechPost (text read from the publisher's own RSS feed; the article page returned HTTP 403); launch date checked on TII's press release as carried by Zawya
key_facts: The Technology Innovation Institute (TII) in Abu Dhabi has released Falcon-ASR, a 1.6B-parameter speech recognition model focused on Emirati Arabic that also transcribes English, French, Spanish and Portuguese with one set of weights.

In TII's evaluation it posts a 20.92% average word error rate across six Arabic test sets, 2.25 points better than the best published entry in TII's leaderboard snapshot (Audar-ASR-V1-Turbo, 23.17%); the figure is TII's own run, not a leaderboard entry.
On an internal, private Emirati and Gulf test set it scores 22.73% WER against 26.80% for the 30B Qwen3-Omni (a 4.07-point lead); because the set is private it cannot be reproduced.
On seven English test sets TII reports a 5.74% mean WER, against 5.76% listed for Qwen3-ASR-1.7B; TII published no scores for French, Spanish or Portuguese.
It returns word-level timestamps, useful for subtitling, searchable recordings and meeting notes.
Access is limited: no weights, license or quantized variants are published; it runs only as a hosted Hugging Face demo (clips up to 60 seconds and 20 MB), with an API and native apps planned.
MarkTechPost could not find a published architecture or training data size; the model builds on TII's Falcon3-Audio work.
TII's press release (Zawya, 6 Oct 2026) announced Falcon-ASR on that date together with the Falcon-Emirati language model and Falcon-OCR-Arabic.
quote_evidence: In TII’s evaluation, Falcon-ASR posts a 20.92% average word error rate (WER) across 6 Arabic test sets.
For developers building Arabic voice products, the catch is access: today it runs only as a hosted demo.
Note that Falcon-ASR’s figure is TII’s own run, not a leaderboard entry.
why_it_matters_hint: A small model that transcribes Emirati dialect more accurately than larger rivals in TII's own tests could improve Arabic subtitles and meeting transcripts, but outsiders cannot yet run or verify it.
event_date: Launch announced by TII on 6 Oct 2026 (Zawya press release); MarkTechPost's benchmark write-up is dated 11 Oct 2026.
notes: MarkTechPost page blocked (HTTP 403); full text read from MarkTechPost's own RSS feed. The 6 Oct 2026 launch date comes from TII's press release on Zawya (page published 2026-10-06), also read. Scores are TII's own evaluation. Not carried in our earlier editions.
